priceSnapshot.note: Nothing happened overnight, and that is the finding. Since the endday snapshot at 63,986.0 the market has traded a 327.0-point box between 63,859.3 and 64,186.3 for six and a half hours and sits 3.5 points lower. Yesterday's 63,750 reduce line was never approached - the overnight low of 63,859.3 stopped 109.3 points above it and 88.1 points above the 4H EMA200 at 63,771.20, which has now survived three separate tests across two sessions without a single settled close beneath it. Two things did change underneath the flat price, and they point in opposite directions. Constructive: open interest ROSE 2.21% to $2,085,719,907 after two consecutive sessions of contraction, and the long/short account ratio finally stopped climbing, printing 1.62 at 04:00Z, 05:00Z, 06:00Z and 07:00Z - four flat hours after three sessions of accounts piling into longs. Destructive: the ETF number the endday session flagged as incomplete came back WORSE, not better. Farside's completed Monday tape shows a net outflow of $144.6m, not the $91.0m partial - IBIT reported and did not rescue the day. So the mechanism the endday worried about is confirmed broken, while the leverage picture stopped deteriorating. Flat price, mixed internals, and a floor that keeps holding.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE below $63,750. UNCHANGED for a third consecutive session, and it has now earned that permanence: the level sits 21.2 points beneath the 4H EMA200 at 63,771.20, and price has probed 63,832.3, 63,818.1 and 63,859.3 across three separate approaches without ever settling an hourly bar under 63,892.9. A settled hourly close below 63,750 means that moving average failed on a close rather than a wick, which removes the last structural floor before the 63,500 shelf and then the 63,000 handle. Everything the wallet holds in cash exists to be deployed above this line; below it, the plan inverts.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE back above $64,650, WITH open interest holding or rising across the same bar. Unchanged from yesterday. The price half is the daily EMA50 at 64,642.26 plus a $2,052,642 realized long-liquidation shelf at 64,600 - the single largest cluster on the 24-hour tape - and the 4H EMA50 at 64,479.71 sits just underneath as the first hurdle. The open-interest half has scored on seven consecutive tests. Note the honest nuance for this session: open interest is now RISING again, so for the first time in three sessions the confirmation clause would probably pass if the price half ever arrived. That makes 64,650 a live trigger rather than a theoretical one.

decisionBox.changed: Position moves from HOLD to ADD. The endday session held 55.53 USDT of cash raised at 63,988.7 specifically to buy a test of the 63,800s, and reasoned that deploying it 136 points above that target into the thinnest liquidity window of the day would waste the trim. That was right. Six hours later the test still has not come, the floor has held a third time, open interest has turned back up and the long/short ratio has stopped climbing - so the risk of waiting has changed character. The seeder deploys a PARTIAL tranche of 20 USDT here and keeps 35.53 USDT dry for a genuine 63,800-63,771 test. The reduce line, the add line and the invalidation are all unchanged.

etfFlows.note: CONFIRMED WORSE. The endday session reported Monday 10 August as a preliminary net OUTFLOW of $91.0m with IBIT still unreported, and named the completed number as the first thing this session should re-read rather than assume. It has been re-read. Farside's completed tape now shows 10 Aug at a net outflow of $144.6m - IBIT reported and did not rescue the day, it deepened it by roughly $54m. That ends five consecutive sessions of net inflows (03 Aug +$170.1m, 04 Aug +$211.5m, 05 Aug +$244.4m, 06 Aug +$137.6m, 07 Aug +$101.7m) and it is the largest single-day outflow since 31 July's -$265.4m. streakDays stays 0. The honest reading: the endday's hopeful caveat was wrong and the desk should say so plainly. Spot demand from the US ETF complex was the mechanism holding the higher-lows structure together since 05 August, and for one session it reversed. One day is not a trend - 31 July printed -$265.4m and was followed immediately by five green days - but it removes the right to treat the ETF bid as a given.

liquidations.note: Over the 988-fill window spanning 2026-08-10T07:34:05Z to 2026-08-11T07:06:49Z, $11,558,117 of LONG liquidations against $34,483 of shorts - a 335 to 1 ratio, and the most one-sided tape the desk has recorded. That headline overstates the present, though, because the window still contains yesterday's flush. The RATE is what matters and the rate has collapsed: the four largest overnight fills since the endday snapshot total roughly $1.5m, against the $10.4m the market force-closed in the six hours to yesterday's midday. Forced selling has effectively stopped for a second consecutive session. The genuinely NEW information is open interest, which ROSE 2.21% to $2,085,719,907 from $2,040,525,808 - the first expansion after two sessions of contraction totalling 1.27%. Rising open interest on flat price means fresh positions are being opened into the box rather than closed out of it, which ends the deleveraging read the last two sessions carried. The long/short account ratio is 1.62 and, critically, FLAT: 1.63 at 04:00Z then 1.62 at 05:00Z, 06:00Z and 07:00Z. Three sessions of accounts adding long exposure into a falling market have stopped adding. Funding is +0.0001 per 8h, about +0.01%, so longs still pay but only nominally. skew is reported as the long/short ACCOUNT ratio (1.62 = longs crowded, downside-vulnerable), consistent with prior sessions, not as the realized long/short USD ratio.

The 63,750 line has now survived three separate approaches across three sessions - lows of 63,832.3, 63,818.1 and 63,859.3 - without a single settled hourly close beneath 63,892.9. The 64,650 add trigger has not fired for eight consecutive sessions and its open-interest confirmation clause has blocked eight would-be entries; note that for the first time in three sessions that clause would now PASS, because open interest is rising again.
calibration.note: priorReduceFired is FALSE and not close: the endday's 63,750 line was never approached, with the overnight low of 63,859.3 stopping 109.3 points above it. actingHelped is set to NULL rather than true or false, deliberately. The endday decision was an explicit HOLD - no trade was placed - so there is no action to score. Marking a no-op as helped or not-helped would pollute the record. What CAN be judged is the reasoning behind it: the endday argued that deploying cash 136 points above the 63,800 shelf into the thinnest window of the day would waste the midday trim, and six hours later the shelf still has not printed and price is 3.5 points lower, so the patience cost nothing and the logic held. That judgement belongs in the narrative, not in this boolean.
